identity.name: Charles Connor
home_scenes: Little Richard's Upsetters on the road
identity.summary: Drummer of Little Richard's road band the Upsetters from 1953, whose drum rhythms Richard said his "a-wop bop-a-loo-mop" referred to.

contribution.description: Little Richard's drummer: playing without a bass player, he thumped the bass drum hard for a "bass fiddle effect", and his four-bar double-shuffle intro to "Keep A-Knockin'" (1957) is the one John Bonham imitated to open "Rock and Roll". James Brown called that band "the first to put funk into the rhythm".

beatbreaker.group: Rock and roll and roots drummers
